questions.passage:
Recording changes in a town square

Researchers studying the daily sound of a town square chose four observation points to capture contrasting surroundings. At the bus entrance they used a directional microphone. This reduced interference from conversations behind the observer, though it meant that the recordings could not represent the whole soundscape around that point.

The cafe frontage presented a different problem. The owner put chairs outside after the first deliveries and moved them indoors before closing. To help explain any sudden changes in sound levels, the observer kept a movement log recording when the chairs were moved.

In the middle of the square, the fountain produced a steady backdrop that could obscure quieter events. The team agreed to record during its scheduled maintenance break as well as during operation. Comparing the recordings helped identify sounds that were still present when the fountain stopped.

At the eastern gate, wind sometimes struck the microphone directly. An observer fitted a foam cover to reduce the resulting noise in the recording. This change improved the recording but did not make the real location quieter.

| Observation point | Method or condition | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bus entrance | [1] ___ | Reduce recorded sound from behind the observer |
| Cafe frontage | [2] ___ | Track when the chairs were moved |
| Fountain | [3] ___ | Listen for other sounds while the fountain is off |
| Eastern gate | [4] ___ | Reduce noise caused by wind hitting the microphone |

questions.passage:
Tracing the use of a printing press

A local archive set out to reconstruct the history of a small printing press. Each type of surviving evidence answered different questions. A set of invoices gave delivery dates for paper. Since several printers bought from the same supplier, the team used an account stamp on each invoice to identify the purchases associated with this press.

Several photograph albums showed the workshop in use. The photos were rarely dated, but researchers sometimes narrowed the period by identifying a wall calendar in the background. A photograph could show a particular layout without revealing how long it had been in place.

The archive also found apprentices’ notebooks. Some included diagrams but no written explanation. Where a page showed a sequence of numbered arrows, researchers used it to infer the order of operations. They kept such inferences separate from direct descriptions in the notes.

Former employees contributed interviews about work routines. To make it easier to find evidence again, the archivists placed a time marker beside each topic heading in the interview catalogue. The markers helped a listener return to the recording rather than relying on a brief written digest.

| Source | Clue or tool | Use in the project |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Invoices | [1] ___ | Identify purchases linked to this press |
| Undated photographs | [2] ___ | Narrow down when a photo was taken |
| Apprentices’ notebooks | [3] ___ | Infer the order of operations |
| Interviews | [4] ___ | Locate discussion of a topic in the recording |
